entries.title: feat(app): enforce single instance with window reactivation
entries.body:
A second launch of Gravityless.exe previously spawned an independent process,
each with its own window, daemon connection and tray icon.

Add a per-user named mutex (Local\Gravityless.Instance.<hash>) that the first
instance holds for its lifetime. A subsequent launch acquires nothing, posts a
registered window message (WM_GRAVITYLESS_ACTIVATE) and exits.

The running instance hooks that message and restores its main window: it clears
the minimized state, calls ShowWindow(SW_RESTORE) and SetForegroundWindow, then
Activate/Focus. Win32 is needed because WPF's Activate alone is refused when
another application owns the foreground.

The protocol branch in OnStartup runs before the mutex check, so
antigravity:// OAuth callbacks still reach the capture route file and never
touch the single-instance path.

Verified: repeated launch keeps one process; a minimized window is restored and
brought to front; a protocol callback exits without affecting the main instance.

entries.title: feat(instances): add project avoidance lock with skip confirmation
entries.body:
A project bound to two instances could be launched twice, and both instances
would then write the same shared SQLite conversation store.

Add InstanceService.FindProjectConflicts, which reports the projects bound to
an instance that another live instance is currently mounting. Ownership is read
from the in-memory _runningProcesses map rather than the persisted
RunningInstanceId, which can survive a crash.

LaunchInstance gains an excludedProjectIds overload. Excluded projects are
skipped for that launch only; InstanceProfile.BoundProjectIds is untouched, so
the next launch sees the full binding again. An empty result is accepted: the
instance starts with no workspace, where the user can still create a project or
open a scratch chat.

The instance page shows a confirmation before launching. When only some
projects conflict, the dialog lists them one per line as "<project> - in use by
<instance>" and the button reads "Skip and start". When every bound project
conflicts, a separate wording explains that the instance opens without projects
and the button reads "Start anyway".

entries.title: feat(projects): hard-link project metadata to a single shared copy
entries.body:
Each instance kept its own copy of config/projects/<id>.json, so the same
project had as many definitions as instances bound to it, and edits made inside
one instance never reached the others.

Add ProjectService.GetProjectConfigJsonPath, which resolves the canonical
metadata file under data/projects/<id>/project.json, and
JunctionService.EnsureFileHardLink, an idempotent link builder that adopts an
existing instance copy as the shared file when the shared one is missing and
falls back to a plain copy when the file system refuses the link.

SetupProjectMetadata now writes the canonical file and hard-links each
instance's copy to it. The shared file is only rewritten when its content
differs, so an unchanged launch does not break and rebuild the link. Deleting
an unbound project's JSON removes only that directory entry, leaving the shared
copy intact.

Hard links are used instead of symbolic links because CreateSymbolicLink needs
Developer Mode or elevation, while hard links need neither. They carry no
reparse point, so IsFileHardLink reads NumberOfLinks through
GetFileInformationByHandle rather than FileAttributes.

Verified against a temporary data root: two instances binding one project
produce three names on a single inode, a rename inside one instance is visible
from the shared file, deleting an instance entry preserves the shared copy, and
a relaunch re-links without duplicating the file.

entries.title: fix(instances): carry SQLite companion files when harvesting conversations
entries.body:
ReconcileAndHarvestProjects moved a conversation database with File.Move, which
leaves the -wal and -shm files behind. In WAL mode a database whose committed
pages still live in -wal loses them on the next open, so a conversation created
inside an instance could come back truncated.

MoveSqliteWithSiblings moves the database and both companions as one unit, and
overwrites a stale target so rows from two databases cannot be mixed.
DeleteSqliteSiblings removes leftovers when the shared copy already exists.

The multi-project mount also drops stale companions before hard-linking a
shared database, otherwise a -wal from an earlier run would be paired with a
database it does not belong to and SQLite would read foreign pages.

Verified against a temporary directory: the -wal content survives the move, the
source directory is left empty, deleting companions keeps the database, and a
database with no companions moves without error.

entries.title: fix(instances): drop stale companions before adopting a harvested database
entries.body:
MoveSqliteWithSiblings cleared the destination database but not its -shm and
-wal, so overwriting an existing shared copy could leave a companion belonging
to the previous occupant next to the incoming database. SQLite would then apply
that stale -shm against a file it was never built for.

Delete the destination companions before the move instead of only handling the
ones the source happens to carry.

Verified with a 22-case harness covering move, overwrite, partial companion
sets, idempotent delete, and the hard-link round trip: all pass.
